claim: (1) The constant c* = 0.76950 32191 50489 43269... of Theorem C is produced exactly by three inequalities: (X) the k = n instance of Lemma 3.1, C(m,n) <= N C(m-h,n), at a bounded number of top levels s = n-i; (Y) the doubling m_s >= 2 m_{s+1} + 1 of Lemma 1.3; (Z) nu_{n-1} >= n+1 of Lemma 1.2. The level-i instance contributes exactly (a_i - 2a_{i-1})/2^i, so the subsystem {X at levels n-2..n-I, Y, Z} has threshold (a_I/2^I + o(1)) n 2^n. The per-level gain tends to n/2, which is the mean of the index t over 0..n-1 in prod_t (m-t)/(m-h-t). (2) Barrier theorem, proved by hand: the whole nu-profile calculus K_n has threshold L*(n) with L*(n)/(n 2^n) -> c* exactly. K_n contains Lemmas 1.1-1.3, every instance of Lemma 3.1 (every level, every k <= n, inside term kept), every instance of Lemma 3.1 applied recursively inside every T[D(A)] (Proposition S: T[D(A)] has S_{n-|A|}), the hereditary constraint |D(A)| >= L*(n-|A|), and the Section 6 (Theorem D) recursion. For every fixed I it is feasible at N = (c_I + o(1)) n 2^n, where c_I = (a_I + 1)/2^I decreases to c*. (3) The structure the task asks to feed in cannot change the limit inside this calculus. The hereditary constraint is implied by the recursive instances (Theorem B4). The recursive instances are implied asymptotically by monotonicity of the integrand (Lemma B1). Even the hypothetical input f(i) >= gamma i 2^i for all i < n, with any gamma > c*, does not let the calculus prove f(n) >= gamma n 2^n for large n (Theorem B5, transport barrier). No improved constant c' > c* is obtained. (4) Upper side, computed exactly. The least Paley primes p = 3 mod 4 with S_n are 7, 19, 67, 331, 1163 for n = 2..6. Every smaller p = 3 mod 4 fails, with a verified undominated n-set. So for 2 <= n <= 6 Paley is below ln2 n^2 2^n and well below the exact random first-moment threshold (21, 91, 311, 931, 2581). The ratio p_n/(n^2 2^n) = 0.44, 0.26, 0.26, 0.41, 0.50 rises from n = 4 on. Nothing asymptotic is proved about Paley beyond Graham-Spencer. The growth rate of f(n) is not determined, and Erdos problem 902 is not solved.

definitions.F, Phi, a_j, c*: As in proof/ERDOS902_PROOF.md section 5: F(x) = x ln x - (x-1) ln(x-1), Phi(a,b) = F(a) - F(a-b) = int_0^1 ln((a-y)/(a-b-y)) dy for a - b >= 1, a_1 = 1, Phi(a_j, a_{j-1}) = ln 2, c* = lim a_j/2^j.
definitions.nu-profile calculus K_n(N): Integer unknowns N = m_0 >= m_1 >= ... >= m_n >= 1. The homogeneous reading is that every s-set A has |D(A)| = m_s, and m_s is the lower bound used for nu_s. Constraints: (Y) m_s >= 2 m_{s+1} + 1 for 0 <= s <= n-1. (Z) m_{n-1} >= n + 1. (R) for every base 0 <= s <= n-1, inner level 0 <= j <= n-s-1 and 1 <= k <= n-s, with t = s + j: m_{s+k} C(m_t, k) <= (m_s - j - m_t) C(m_t - m_{t+1}, k) + m_t C(m_t - m_{t+1} - 1, k). Base s = 0 is Lemma 3.1 in T at every level and every k. Base s >= 1 is Lemma 3.1 applied inside T[D(A)], |A| = s, which has order m_s, property S_{n-s}, and inner dominator numbers nu^{D(A)}_k >= nu_{s+k}. (F) the hereditary constraint m_s >= L*(n-s) for 1 <= s <= n-1. Lemma 1.2 inside every D(A), the minimum in-degree statement of Lemma 1.3 inside every D(A), and every lambda_k used by the Section 6 recursion are implied by (Y), (Z) and (R).
definitions.L*(n): The least N with K_n(N) non-empty, defined by induction on n because of (F). X_D(n) is the threshold of the Section 6 recursion (Theorem D). Then X_D(n) <= L*(n), by the downward-induction argument of Section 6: a feasible profile dominates the recursion's L_s.
definitions.barrier profile P_n^(I): m_n = 1, m_{n-1} = n + 2. For 2 <= i <= I: m_{n-i} = ceil(n A_i), where A_i is the unique root in (2b, 2b+1) of Phi(A, b) = ln 2 with b = (m_{n-i+1} + 1)/n. For 0 <= s < n - I: m_s = 2 m_{s+1} + n + 2. N_n^(I) = m_0 = 2^(n-I)(m_{n-I} + n + 2) - (n + 2).
definitions.Proposition S: If T has S_n and |A| = s <= n-1, then T[D(A)] has S_{n-s}, and for U contained in D(A), the dominators of U inside T[D(A)] are exactly D(A union U).
definitions.p_n: The least prime p = 3 mod 4 such that the Paley tournament QR_p (x -> y iff y - x is a nonzero square) has S_n.
definitions.first-moment threshold: The least N with C(N,n)(1 - 2^-n)^(N-n) < 1. A uniformly random tournament on N vertices then has S_n with positive probability, so f(n) <= this N. This is rigorous.

argument:
PART 1. WHERE c* COMES FROM.
Theorem C uses exactly three facts. (Z) nu_{n-1} >= n+1 gives a_1 = 1. (X) Lemma 3.1 with k = n and nu_n >= 1 at the minimiser of level s = n-i reads C(m,n) <= N C(m-h,n). Lemma 5.2 turns it into Phi((m+1)/n, h/n) < ln2 + (ln n)/n, which is used only for bounded i. (Y) doubling (2) carries level n-I down to level 0. The constant ln 2 enters only as lim (ln N)/n, so any N = 2^(n+o(1)n) gives the same equation. Expanding F(x) = ln x + 1 - 1/(2x) + O(x^-2) gives Phi(2b + g, b) = ln 2 + (1/2 - g)/(2b) + O(b^-2). So the level gain g = a_i - 2a_{i-1} tends to 1/2. In the discrete count this 1/2 is the mean of t over 0..n-1 in sum_t ln((m-t)/(m-h-t)) = n ln 2 + sum_t (t - g n)/(2h) + ... Computed values of a_i - 2a_{i-1}: 0.5622, 0.5244, 0.5111, 0.5053, 0.5026, ... = 1/2 + O(2^-i). Hence c* = 1/2 + sum_{i>=2} (a_i - 2a_{i-1})/2^i = 0.75 + 0.0195.
Proposition B0 (exact accounting). For fixed I, consider the subsystem {X at levels n-2..n-I, Y, Z}. Lower bound: Lemma 5.3 for i <= I, then (2), gives liminf >= a_I/2^I. Upper bound: take the top values of P_n^(I) and pure doubling m_s = 2m_{s+1} + 1 below level n - I. By Lemma B1's computation, C(m,n)/C(m-h-1,n) <= 2^n <= N - s at the top levels, since N >= 2^(n-I) m_{n-I} >> 2^n + n. Then N = 2^(n-I)(m_{n-I} + 1) - 1 = (a_I/2^I + o(1)) n 2^n. So the subsystem threshold is exactly (a_I/2^I + o(1)) n 2^n.

PART 2. THE BARRIER.
Lemma B1 (sufficient condition). Let n >= 1 and integers N = m_0 > ... > m_n = 1 satisfy, for 0 <= t <= n-1: (i) m_t - m_{t+1} - 1 >= n; (ii) Phi(m_t/n, (m_{t+1}+1)/n) <= ln 2; (iii) m_t - 2m_{t+1} >= max(1, n-t-1); and (iv) m_{n-1} >= n+1. Then (Y), (Z) and every instance of (R) hold.
Proof. Fix s, j, k and put t = s+j, m = m_t, h = m_{t+1}. Then C(m,k)/C(m-h-1,k) = exp(sum_{u<k} g(u)) with g(x) = ln((m-x)/(m-h-1-x)). By (i), g is finite and increasing on [0, k), since k <= n <= m-h-1. So sum_{u<k} g(u) <= int_0^k g = n int_0^{k/n} psi, where psi(y) = ln((alpha - y)/(alpha - beta - y)), alpha = m/n, beta = (h+1)/n and alpha - beta >= 1. psi is increasing, so its average over [0, k/n] is at most its average over [0,1]. Hence sum <= k Phi(alpha, beta) <= k ln 2 by (ii), and C(m,k) <= 2^k C(m-h-1,k). By (iii) all gaps m_u - 2m_{u+1} are nonnegative, so m_s - 2^k m_{s+k} = sum_{u=s}^{s+k-1} 2^(u-s)(m_u - 2m_{u+1}) >= m_s - 2m_{s+1} >= n-s-1 >= j. Also m_s - j - m_t >= 0: this is trivial for j = 0, and for j >= 1, m_s - m_t >= m_s - m_{s+1} > n > j. Therefore LHS = m_{s+k} C(m,k) <= 2^k m_{s+k} C(m-h-1,k) <= (m_s - j) C(m-h-1,k) <= (m_s - j - m) C(m-h,k) + m C(m-h-1,k) = RHS. (Y) follows from (iii), and (Z) is (iv). QED
Theorem B2 (barrier). For every fixed I >= 2 there is n_0(I) such that for n >= n_0(I), P_n^(I) satisfies (i)-(iv). Hence K_n(N_n^(I)) holds without (F), and with (F) by B4. Moreover N_n^(I)/(n 2^n) -> c_I.
Proof. Top levels 2 <= i <= I: b = (m_{n-i+1}+1)/n >= (n+3)/n >= 1, so A_i exists and lies in (2b, 2b+1) by Lemma 5.1 (i)-(iii). (ii) holds because ceil(nA_i)/n >= A_i and Phi decreases in a. (i) holds because m - h - 1 >= nA_i - h - 1 > 2(h+1) - h - 1 = h + 1 >= n + 3. For (iii), the root map b -> A(b) is continuous (Phi is continuous and strictly decreasing in a), so by induction m_{n-i}/n -> a_i. Since a_i > 2a_{i-1}, the gap m_{n-i} - 2m_{n-i+1} >= (a_i - 2a_{i-1}) n/2 >= I > i-1 for large n. Level n-1: gap n, (i) holds with equality n, and Phi = F(1 + 2/n) <= ln 2 for n >= 7 (F(9/7) = 0.6811). Deep levels s < n-I: gap n+2 gives (i) and (iii), and m_s/n = 2b + 1 with b = (m_{s+1}+1)/n >= 1 gives Phi(2b+1, b) < ln 2 by Lemma 5.1(ii). The limit: N/(n 2^n) = (m_{n-I}/n + 1 + 2/n) 2^-I - (n+2)/(n 2^n) -> (a_I + 1)/2^I. QED
Corollary B3. L*(n)/(n 2^n) -> c*. Proof: the proof of Theorem C (Lemmas 5.2, 5.3 and (2)) uses only constraints of K_n, so liminf >= c*; B2 gives limsup <= c_I for every I. Also X_D(n) <= L*(n) <= N_n^(I).
Theorem B4 (hereditary constraint is redundant). If (m_0, ..., m_n) satisfies (Y), (Z) and (R) of K_n, then every tail (m_s, ..., m_n) satisfies (Y), (Z) and (R) of K_{n-s}. The tail's instances of (R) are the instances of K_n with base >= s, and its (Z) is m_{n-1} >= n-s+1. By induction on n, the tail lies in K_{n-s}(m_s), so m_s >= L*(n-s), and (F) is automatic. QED
Proposition S. Let |A| = s <= n-1, R = D(A) and U a subset of R with |U| = n-s. Then A union U is an n-set (R and A are disjoint), so it has a dominator w outside it. w beats A, so w is in R, w is not in U, and w beats U. Conversely, a w in R minus U that beats U lies in D(A union U). So D_{T[R]}(U) = D(A union U), T[R] has S_{n-s}, |D(A)| >= f(n-s), and nu^{T[R]}_k >= nu_{s+k}. These are exactly the facts encoded in (R) and (F). Checked by brute force on QR_7, QR_19 and QR_67 (29 855 subsets). QED
Theorem B5 (transport barrier). Let gamma > c*. For all large n there is a profile satisfying K_n together with the hypothetical inputs m_s >= phi_s := ceil(gamma (n-s) 2^(n-s)) for 1 <= s <= n-1, and with N = m_0 < gamma n 2^n. So inside the calculus, |D(A)| >= f(n-|A|) cannot close an induction 'f(i) >= gamma i 2^i for all i < n implies f(n) >= gamma n 2^n' for any gamma > c*.
Proof. Choose I with c_I < gamma. For s >= n-I take the values of P_n^(I); for large n these are >= phi_s, since phi_s <= gamma I 2^I is bounded and m_s >= n. For 1 <= s < n-I put m_s = max(2m_{s+1} + n + 2, phi_s), and put m_0 = 2m_1 + n + 2. Every deep gap is >= n+2, so Lemma B1 applies. Write u_s = m_s + n + 2. Then u_s = max(2u_{s+1}, phi_s + n + 2), so u_1 <= max(2^(n-I-1) u_{n-I}, max_t f(t)) with f(t) = gamma (n-t) 2^(n-1) + 2^(t-1)(n+3). f is convex, so its maximum is at t = 1 or t = n-I-1, and f(n-I-1) <= f(1) for large n because 2^(-I-1) < 1/2 < gamma. Hence N = 2u_1 - (n+2) <= max(N_n^(I), gamma (n-1) 2^n + n + 4) < gamma n 2^n for large n. QED
Why the ignored structure cannot help (summary). (a) Inner counts in T[D(A)] replace (N, nu_k) by (|D(A)|, nu_{s+k}). After the integral comparison they read k Phi <= k ln 2. This is the k-fraction of the outer k = n inequality, because the integrand ln((alpha-y)/(alpha-beta-y)) increases in y, so they add nothing. (b) |D(A)| >= f(n-s) is a tail-feasibility statement, and tails of a feasible profile are feasible (B4). (c) Near the bottom (s small) it is equivalent to doubling, and doubling leaves an additive slack of only n+2 per level, which B5 exhibits.
Lemma 3.1' (degree form, proved). C(x,k)/x is nondecreasing in x for k >= 1, and sum_{y not in A} |N+(y) cap R| = sum_{r in R} d-(r), because no vertex of A beats R. Hence nu_k C(m,k) <= C(m-h,k)/(m-h) * sum_{r in R} d-(r). For near-regular T (all d- <= ceil((N-1)/2)) this is checked in exact integers on the barrier profiles for n = 16..256 at every level and every k, and it always holds. So in-degree information of this kind does not separate the barrier either. This part is a computation, not a hand proof.

PART 3. WHAT THE CALCULUS CANNOT SEE (heuristic). The calculus records only sizes. At level i, the sets Q_y = D(A + y) = D(A) cap N-(y) must jointly satisfy two conditions. First, their complements in R cover every n-subset of R; this is what the count uses. Second, |Q_{y_1} cap ... cap Q_{y_j}| = |D(A + y_1 + ... + y_j)| >= nu_{n-i+j} for j <= i; this is NOT used. r8f_intersect.py compares exponential rates. If the Q_y were uniformly random sets of the extremal sizes, then at every level i >= 3 a typical Q_y would lie in about e^{0.65 n} pairs (and e^{1.3 n} triples) violating the intersection bounds. Already for pairs, the required intersection a_{i-2} n is only slightly below the random mean a_{i-1}^2/a_i n (1.000 vs 1.162 at i = 3), while there are e^{2n ln 2} pairs. At i = 2 the exponent is exactly 0: P(two random n-sets in a_2 n points are disjoint) equals the covering probability, and this borderline case is just Lemma 1.2. So any S_n tournament near c* n 2^n would need extremely non-random dominator families. This joint covering-plus-intersection structure is the only place found where a constant above c* could come from. It is not proved that it does.

PART 4. UPPER SIDE. Proved in the literature: f(n) <= (ln 2 + o(1)) n^2 2^n (Erdos 1963, first moment). Explicit: Graham-Spencer 1971, QR_p has S_n for p = 3 mod 4 prime with p > n^2 2^(2n-2); this rests on a character-sum (Weil) bound and gives an explicit family of order about n^2 4^n. The repository's note that random Cayley or G-invariant tournaments cannot beat ln 2 is cited in proof section 8.3, but its source file is missing (COUNTEREXAMPLES.md). Computed here: exact least Paley primes and the random first-moment thresholds; see evidence. Heuristic only: Paley behaves like a random tournament for small dominating sets. The rising ratio p_n/(n^2 2^n) is compatible with p_n ~ ln2 n^2 2^n, but five data points decide nothing. No explicit family is known to me that provably beats (ln 2) n^2 2^n, or even O(n^2 2^n).

weaknesses: The barrier (B2-B5) is a statement about the nu-profile calculus. It covers inequalities whose only quantities are N and minimum dominator-set sizes, applied at every level and recursively inside every D(A), under the homogeneous reading that every s-set has m_s dominators. It does not cover arguments that use how the sets D(A + y) intersect jointly, the distribution of |N+(y) cap D(A)| beyond its maximum, global averaging identities such as sum_{|A|=s} |D(A)| = sum_v C(d+(v), s) (the homogeneous reading actually violates the lower bound this identity gives on the average at top levels, but lower-bound proofs only use minimisers), spectral information, or anything specific to small n. Such arguments could still beat c*.

Theorem B5 covers hypothetical inductive inputs of the form gamma i 2^i, and also gamma i 2^i + K 2^i when K < gamma. It does not exclude an induction with a different shape, for example inputs that grow like i^2 2^i. Those would have to come from outside the calculus, because the calculus cannot prove them.
n_0(I) in Theorem B2 is not made explicit. The exact checks show feasibility from n = 8 on with the best I, and show that the Lemma B1 hypotheses hold for n >= 80.
Lemma 3.1' (degree form) is proved, but its harmlessness for near-regular T is only computed (n = 16..256), not proved by hand.

Part 3 (joint intersection structure) is heuristic. It compares exponential rates for uniformly random families, with exact hypergeometric rates for pairs and a binomial approximation for j >= 3. It proves nothing about tournaments, and the statement that intersecting families add nothing at level 2 is only a sketch.

The Paley results rely on single implementations (numpy float32 products of 0/1 matrices, exact below 2^24) and on the arc-transitivity reduction. Witnesses are re-verified independently, but the positive results (S_5 for QR_331, S_6 for QR_1163) have not been reproduced by a second program. I did not check whether p_5 = 331 and p_6 = 1163 already appear in the literature. They give f(5) <= 331 and f(6) <= 1163 only by exhibition.
The Graham-Spencer condition p > n^2 2^(2n-2) is quoted from memory of the 1971 paper and was not re-opened in this task.

next_step: Stop working inside the nu-profile calculus: B2-B5 show that it is exactly saturated at c*. The only candidate found for a constant above c* is the joint set-system structure at a single level i >= 3. Formulate it as an extremal problem and bound it, under the suggested approach key level3-intersecting-covering. Problem P_3: R has a n points; a weighted family of subsets Q (each |Q| >= a_2 n) has total weight 2^(n+o(n)); every n-subset of R misses some Q; any two members meet in >= n points and any three in >= 1 point. Is the least such a strictly larger than a_3 = 5.6487? A strict increase would raise c* by at least (increase)/8. Suggested tools: a Delsarte-type LP or flag-algebra SDP over the intersection-size distribution of pairs, and the Frankl-Rodl forbidden-intersection theorem for the pair condition (all intersections below n are forbidden). Check numerically on scaled-down instances before attempting a proof. Separately, an independent program should confirm S_6 for QR_1163 and the witness list below it.
